sources.title: One million people have mapped their mobile – have you?
sources.evidence_kind: mobile checker adoption and methodology information
sources.evidence_location: official HTML milestone and checker-method sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom postcode and postal-district views
facts: Ofcom reported one million users of Map Your Mobile
Users enter a postcode to compare network availability in an area
The tool shows a provider-performance score for the postal district
The checker combines crowdsourced Opensignal data with network predictions
limitations: Postal-district scores are not parcel-level fixed broadband evidence
Predicted and crowdsourced mobile observations are not live orderability

sources.title: Quicker complaints resolution for telecoms customers, under new Ofcom rules
sources.evidence_location: official HTML evidence and decision sections
facts: Ofcom reduced the ADR access timeframe from eight weeks to six weeks
The change took effect on 8 April 2026
Ofcom reported 79% of major-provider complaints were resolved within one week in the analysed period
Ofcom reported 94% were resolved within six weeks in the analysed period
limitations: Complaint-resolution timing is not network coverage
Historical complaint handling evidence is not provider orderability

sources.title: Quicker complaints resolution and more money in your pocket when things go wrong
sources.evidence_location: official HTML ADR and compensation sections
facts: The six-week ADR access rule was live from 8 April 2026
ADR bodies independently assess unresolved customer-provider disputes
The prior ADR access period was eight weeks
Automatic compensation payouts increase with inflation
limitations: Consumer-redress entitlement is not coverage evidence
Compensation and dispute rules do not identify an available package

sources.title: Report: Complaints about broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV services
sources.evidence_kind: quarterly provider complaint-rate dataset and report
sources.evidence_location: official HTML methodology and overall-trends sections
facts: Provider complaint rates are normalised per 100,000 customers
Q1 2026 covers January to March 2026
Total complaints decreased compared with Q4 2025
Fixed broadband and pay-monthly mobile complaints decreased
limitations: Complaint rates are not coverage or performance measurements
Only providers meeting publication criteria are compared

sources.title: Comparing customer service: choosing the best home broadband, mobile and landline provider
sources.published: current report index; restatement notice April 2026
sources.evidence_kind: annual customer-service report and data-quality notice
sources.evidence_location: official HTML restatement notice and report index
facts: EE resubmitted certain 2024 broadband and landline faults information in April 2026
Ofcom identified affected EE faults data and associated industry averages
The 2025 report was expected to be reissued after review
The page separates full report, interactive report and annexes
limitations: Data under restatement must not be treated as final
Customer-service metrics do not prove parcel coverage
